editorial:
The Joe Louis Story is a 1953 United Artists biopic of the heavyweight champion. Robert Gordon directed and Stirling Silliphant produced. Robert Sylvester wrote the screenplay and George Bassman composed the music. Coley Wallace plays Louis, with Hilda Simms, Paul Stewart and James Edwards in support. Wikipedia's infobox gives the production company as 'Walter P. Chrysler Jr.', which is a person's name. I could not check it against the AFI Catalog or the film's credits. The film opened in the US on September 18, 1953. An 88-minute black-and-white copy is listed on the Internet Archive.

The film is not confirmed as public domain. A film from 1953 is free only if it was published without a notice or its copyright was not renewed. The renewal year is 1981 (the 28th year). Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes or catalog entries from 1982 may list late-published 1981 renewals, so check both years' records, but 1982 is not a renewal window. I have not searched the Copyright Office renewal records or a Catalog of Copyright Entries volume for this film. The one renewal hit in our queue, RE0000111481 (1981), is titled 'The Joe Louis story' and its claimants are the Louis family. Our script catalogued it as music/other, and I did not view the record itself. It is probably a separate underlying work, and its relation to the film is unknown. Check it and the film's own record before you reuse the picture or its music. Whether the film has a separate underlying story or book is also open. A colorized 4K upload also exists on the Internet Archive, and that version adds material that may carry its own protection.
